findings.F1: The learned combination points the wrong way on unseen dates. Its post-pipeline score correlates -0.032 with the next 5-day return net of drift (3254 non-overlapping cases), and the best-single copy correlates -0.034. Its top quintile earns +0.09 % against +0.76 % for its bottom quintile (t -1.11), and its fourth quintile is the lowest at -0.97 % (t -2.47).
findings.F2: The book lost on timing, not on drift. Its position held a mean of -0.18 to +0.01 of the book and was long only 41 to 53 % of bars. Timing was negative on 5 of 6 coins, from -0.04 to -0.10 % per day, against drift contributions of at most 0.02 % per day.
findings.F3: The raw single signals, unweighted, point the right way while the learned combination does not. The 28-day return has a Pearson correlation of +0.059 with the next 5-day return, top minus bottom quintile +1.65 % (t 2.21). The volatility-scaled 1-day return has +0.051, top minus bottom +1.78 % (t 2.81, 2432 cases). The 1-day return therefore continues rather than reverses, the opposite of the brief's assumed short reversal. It also correlates -0.152 with the combined score.
findings.F4: Neither single signal is stable across periods. The volatility-scaled 1-day signal's signed-rank t is 1.51 overall, 2.42 in w1-12 and 0.03 in w13-24, and runs from 4.11 in 2019 to -2.08 in 2025. The 28-day signal's is 1.31 overall, with yearly t from -1.14 to 2.03. Neither stands out once the many angles looked at are counted.
findings.F5: Saturday's daily return is the highest of the week. It averages +0.31 % above the coin's mean (t 3.78, 2365 days) and is above the rest of the week on all 6 coins (+0.04 % to +0.51 %, t vs rest 0.34 to 2.67) and in 6 of 8 years. Thursday (-0.32 %, t -2.87) and Tuesday (-0.23 %, t -2.43) are the lowest.
findings.F6: The Saturday rise grows with the coin's return over the preceding 7 days. By quintile of that return, Saturday's demeaned return is -0.13 %, -0.29 %, +0.13 %, +0.48 % (t 2.94) and +1.29 % (t 4.42, 360 days). In volatility units that is a mean z of +0.05, -0.08, +0.03, +0.15 and +0.28. The top quintile's move is about 6.8 times the 0.19 % round-trip cost.
findings.F7: Grouping Saturdays by the prior day's volatility, return or volume gives no ordered pattern. By prior 30-day volatility the quintile means are +0.35, +0.48, -0.12, +0.57 and +0.21 %. Only the prior week's return grades the Saturday move.
findings.F8: The size of the next 5-day move rises steadily with 30-day volatility. The mean absolute move is 5.7 %, 6.1 %, 6.5 %, 7.3 % and 10.0 % from the lowest to the highest volatility quintile. The direction of the move does not follow volatility: quintile means run from -0.30 % to +0.57 %, with t no larger than 0.91.

ideas.idea: On a Saturday, a coin's return over the next day is larger the higher its return over the preceding 7 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long into the weekend on coins that rose over the past week, in proportion to that rise, and stay out of those that fell.
ideas.name: weekend continuation after strong week

ideas.idea: A coin's return over the next day is higher on Saturday than on its other days of the week, and higher the more the coin rose over the preceding 7 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would place a coin's weekly long exposure on the Saturday, sized up after a strong week, rather than spread it evenly across the week.
ideas.name: Saturday drift scaled by week
